fieldValues.title: 8. Decide: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached:
The ideal: Choices that govern later choices are made at the right level by the right owner, in a form they can judge, recorded once and cited, never asked again.

What we have tried: The decision log and its four tests; the seven decision kinds; decision modes, Doors and the Pattern Grid (srs); ADRs and ADR-048 (srs-rust); sessions, quorum and ratification; the owner desk; the affirmation layer (srs-web#617); the decision-taxonomy exercise (2026-10-22).

Problems recorded here: SP-42, SP-63, SP-64, SP-69, SP-91, SP-92, SP-93, SP-99, SP-100, SP-104.
fieldValues.tensions:
- Line 2, Case by case and a standing rule: too far toward Case by case. The owner receives more decisions than they can judge (SP-63); the owner cannot tell what is asked of them (SP-100).
- Model B corrects model A: deciding is not the bottleneck (83 ratified, 5 proposed). The weak points are execution (SP-02: relation rules ratified 12 weeks earlier, never enforced) and form (SP-115).
- The stage's other two tensions stay as records under its domain, out of this map (one trade-off per stage, owner, 2026-10-25).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions:
